mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds has the greater formula mass?

options.C: Both have the same formula mass
options.D: Cannot be determined without experimental data

mcqs.explanation: Formula mass is the sum of the relative atomic masses of all atoms in the formula. CaCO3 = 40.08 (Ca) + 12.01 (C) + 3×16.00 (O) = 100.09 u. Al2(SO4)3 = 2×26.98 (Al) + 3×32.07 (S) + 12×16.00 (O) = 342.15 u. Therefore Al2(SO4)3 has the greater formula mass.

mcqs.learning_point: Use relative atomic masses in chemical calculations
mcqs.question: In the reaction 2 Na + Cl₂ → 2 NaCl, if 2.00 g of sodium react with excess chlorine, what mass of sodium chloride is formed? (Relative atomic masses: Na = 22.99, Cl = 35.45)
mcqs.explanation: Moles of Na = 2.00 g / 22.99 g mol⁻¹ = 0.0870 mol. From the balanced equation, 1 mol Na produces 1 mol NaCl. Molar mass of NaCl = 22.99 + 35.45 = 58.44 g mol⁻¹. Mass of NaCl formed = 0.0870 mol × 58.44 g mol⁻¹ = 5.08 g (rounded to two decimal places).

mcqs.question: What is the correct definition of atomic mass as used in chemistry?

options.A: The mass of a single atom of an element expressed in kilograms.
options.B: The weighted average mass of all naturally occurring isotopes of an element relative to 1/12 of the mass of a carbon‑12 atom.
options.C: The mass number of the most abundant isotope of the element.
options.D: The mass of an atom expressed in grams per mole.

mcqs.answer: The weighted average mass of all naturally occurring isotopes of an element relative to 1/12 of the mass of a carbon‑12 atom.
mcqs.explanation: Atomic mass is not the mass of a single atom but the average mass of all isotopes of an element, weighted by their natural abundances, and expressed relative to 1/12 the mass of a carbon‑12 atom. This definition distinguishes it from mass number (which is an integer for a specific isotope).

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes one atomic mass unit (amu)?

options.A: 1 amu is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon‑12 atom.
options.B: 1 amu equals the mass of a hydrogen atom.
options.C: 1 amu is the mass of one mole of carbon atoms.
options.D: 1 amu is the same as 1 gram.

mcqs.answer: 1 amu is defined as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon‑12 atom.
mcqs.explanation: The atomic mass unit is defined as 1/12 of the mass of a neutral carbon‑12 atom. This provides a convenient scale for expressing relative atomic masses of all elements. Options B, C, and D are incorrect definitions.

mcqs.question: Calculate the molecular mass of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆.
mcqs.explanation: Molecular mass = 6×12.01 (C) + 12×1.008 (H) + 6×16.00 (O) = 72.06 + 12.10 + 96.00 = 180.16 u. This is the sum of the relative atomic masses of all atoms in one molecule of glucose.

mcqs.question: What is the formula mass of iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃? (Relative atomic masses: Fe = 55.85, O = 16.00)
mcqs.explanation: Formula mass = 2×55.85 (Fe) + 3×16.00 (O) = 111.70 + 48.00 = 159.70 u, rounded to 159.7 u. This is the sum of the relative atomic masses of the atoms present in the empirical formula.

mcqs.learning_point: Use relative atomic masses in chemical calculations
mcqs.question: Using relative atomic masses (Na = 22.99, Cl = 35.45), calculate the mass percent of chlorine in sodium chloride (NaCl).
mcqs.explanation: Mass of Cl = 35.45 u, total mass of NaCl = 22.99 u + 35.45 u = 58.44 u. Mass percent of Cl = (35.45 / 58.44) × 100 = 60.66 %, which rounds to 60.7 %. The other options are incorrect calculations.

mcqs.question: A scientist is determining the atomic mass of element X by measuring the relative abundances of its isotopes. Which definition of atomic mass best reflects the quantity the scientist is calculating?

options.A: The mass of the most abundant isotope of element X.
options.B: The average mass of all isotopes of element X weighted by their natural abundances, expressed relative to 1/12 the mass of a carbon‑12 atom.
options.C: The mass number of the heaviest isotope of element X.
options.D: The mass of a single atom of element X in kilograms.

mcqs.answer: The average mass of all isotopes of element X weighted by their natural abundances, expressed relative to 1/12 the mass of a carbon‑12 atom.
mcqs.explanation: When isotopic abundances are considered, the atomic mass is the weighted average of the masses of all naturally occurring isotopes, referenced to 1/12 the mass of a carbon‑12 atom. Options A, C, and D describe other concepts (most abundant isotope, mass number, absolute mass) that are not the definition of atomic mass used in chemistry.
